subject: Clarify streaming measurement methodology and remedy scope
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@acme-bio.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-20T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: measurement approach for streaming latency & concurrency

Sam — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on how Redwood would measure streaming latency, and how that flows into SLA language. Short version up top, details below.

Top asks / outcomes we agreed to:
- Acme: target p95 tail <= 300ms for single-client interactive streaming (web UI) and p95 <= 200ms for internal batch gRPC consumers.
- Redwood: propose measurement windows, synthetic vs. production sampling, and a list of exclusions.
- Next step: we’ll share a short CSV with sample event-level latency and a draft SLA clause describing measurement and remedies.

Measurement approach (proposed)
- Unit of measurement: per-API-request end-to-end streaming tail latency measured from first client request byte to final token streamed completion acknowledgement. For streaming we capture both initial-response latency and total completion latency; SLA attaches to completion latency.
- Percentiles: use rolling 7d p95 & p99 for SLA evaluation, and daily p95 for operational alerts.
- Concurrency accounting: concurrency is tracked per-customer rolling-average over 1-minute buckets; spikes above configured reserved capacity will be considered capacity events (see exclusions).
- Synthetic vs production: primary reporting will use production-sampled telemetry (1% by default) plus a synthetic load harness for validation during onboarding.

Exclusions we propose to include in contract language
- Planned maintenance windows with >=48h notice.
- Customer-side networking incidents (AS-paths outside Redwood control).
- Denial-of-service or traffic surges >5x baseline if not coordinated as burst traffic.

Remedies (draft)
- Monthly service credits proportional to hours of SLA breach for the model endpoint up to a cap of 10% of monthly committed fees.
- Root-cause report and remediation plan for repeated breaches (>3 in 90d).

Attachments: we attached a small sample of event data (acme_latency_sample.csv) and a first-pass SLA wording (redwood-slo-proposal-v1.pdf).

Questions for you:
1) Do the measurement units and percentile windows match what Acme expects?
2) For concurrency, do you want per-client-driver limits (e.g., per user session) or account-level concurrency?
3) Are there specific maintenance blackout windows we should honor?

If that looks reasonable I’ll get Ben & Aditya to draft the final clause and include the measurement query we’ll use to reproduce the numbers.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0198

From: Sam Park <sam.park@acme-bio.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+acme-bio@example.com
Date: 2027-03-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: measurement approach for streaming latency & concurrency

Laura — thanks, this is helpful. A couple clarifications from our side:

1) Targets: the interactive web UI target is accurate (p95 <= 300ms). For our internal gRPC consumers the p95 target is actually <= 150ms during normal batch windows; we can accept a separate SLA tier for batch pipelines for the first 90 days.

2) Concurrency: we care about both. Our main concern is account-level concurrency (multiple parallel sessions across teams), but we also want a hard per-session cap to prevent a single client hogging KV cache slots. Can Redwood support both dimensions in reporting?

3) Exclusions: agreed on planned maintenance and customer-side network. For DDoS we want a clear runbook: if the attack originates outside our ASN but impacts tail, it should count toward an incident unless we engaged Redwood mitigation. Can we add that to the exclusions notes?

We reviewed the CSV snapshot and it looks consistent. Can you also share the query you use to compute p95 and whether you use weighted sampling for streaming sessions that vary in token count?

— Sam
Sam Park
Engineering Lead, Platform
Acme Bio
sam.park@acme-bio.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@acme-bio.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-21T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: measurement approach for streaming latency & concurrency

Sam — great notes. Answers inline below and a short ask at the end.

1) Targets: we can split tiers — will reflect p95 <= 300ms for interactive and p95 <= 150ms for batch gRPC in the draft clause.

2) Concurrency: yes, Redwood can report both per-account and per-session concurrency. Implementation note: per-session caps require instrumentation on the client session ID; if you can guarantee a stable session id in the request metadata we’ll generate both graphs. For SLA evaluation concurrency thresholds are account-level by default; per-session limits will be treated as protective throttles and not directly in the SLA unless we add them as a separate clause.

3) DDoS exclusion: we can add an explicit line: \"Incidents caused by third-party volumetric attacks are excluded from SLA credit unless Redwood's mitigation service was engaged and failed to contain the attack.\" We’ll iterate wording with your security contact.

Regarding the p95 computation and sampling: our default is production-sampled events with equal weighting per request (not per token). For streaming sessions with variable token counts we include an optional weighted-percentile that normalizes by final token count — we can provide both numbers in reports. The p95 used for SLA will be the request-equal metric unless you ask us to use token-weighted percentile.

Action items we’ll take this week:
- Ben: draft refined SLA paragraph that calls out dual-tier targets, percentile windows, and exclusions (deliver EOD Wed).
- Aditya: share the exact SQL/promQL queries we use to compute p95 & p99 and a short Jupyter notebook that reproduces the CSV.
- Laura: propose a 2-week onboarding test window where Redwood will run a synthetic harness (link in related_links) that mirrors your production mix; we’ll log both synthetic and production-sampled metrics side-by-side.

If you confirm the token-weighting preference (request-equal vs token-weighted for SLA) we’ll lock the wording.

— Laura

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sam Park <sam.park@acme-bio.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-22T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: measurement approach for streaming latency & concurrency

Sam / team — looping in a couple implementation details and a draft remediation schedule so the sales/legal teams have concrete language to work with.

Measurement queries (high level)
- p95_request_equal: SELECT percentile_disc(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY request_latency_ms) FROM streaming_events WHERE customer_id = :id AND time >= now() - interval '7 days' AND sample = true;
- p95_token_weighted: compute per-request latency * token_count, aggregate and compute weighted percentile; we’ll include sample code in the notebook.

On remedies and credits (draft)
- Remediation tiers:
  * Single incident (SLO breach in a calendar month): 5% service credit for affected endpoint for that month.
  * Repeated breaches (>=3 breaches in 90 days): 10% credit and mandatory joint RCA within 10 business days.
  * Catastrophic failure (global outage >4 hours): escalation to leadership and potential credit beyond 10% by negotiation.
- Cap: credits capped at 10% of monthly committed fees unless otherwise negotiated on enterprise contract.

Operational reporting cadence
- Weekly operational digest: per-endpoint p95/p99, top contributing request paths, and concurrency percentiles.
- Monthly SLA report: rolling 7d p95/p99 windows, list of exclusions applied, and credit calculations if any.

Next steps / ask
- Sam: confirm whether Acme prefers request-equal p95 for SLA or token-weighted.
- Legal: will want the exclusion wording tightened around DDoS and coordinated bursts; we flagged that.
- Ops: we can stand up a 2-week synthetic run starting 2027-03-29 if you want to give us a production traffic replay.

I’ll convert the remedies bullets into contract language and send to Ben for the pricing attachment.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Principal Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
